A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite the renamed title and method. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: v1 reports original speedup experiments, parameter sweeps and quality-speed measurements on four benchmarks in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds parallel-baseline comparisons, component ablations, absolute throughput measurements and NPU results.

M1.justification: Speculative Ensemble becomes CoS, and speculative-based ensemble becomes Naive-CoS. The verification/resampling rule, bonus-token alternation and multi-model procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2.

E1.justification: Both evaluate HumanEval, GSM8K, MMLU and CNNDM for the same four tasks. Added ablations and hardware evaluations reuse this coverage. Decoding-time realignment is newly discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 adds parallel collaborative decoding, WE-P/CD-P, to the comparisons in Tables 2–3. Tables 7–8 also introduce no-APF comparators; v2 identifies the CD variant as equivalent to SCD, which v1 only discussed. These substantially expand the evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: v2 adds an Ascend 910B3 execution setting and APF-removal evaluation conditions. Existing model pairs, combination weights, temperatures and proposal-length selection remain unchanged. Newly specified GPU hardware documents existing experiments without establishing that their settings changed or they were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4 adds direct ablations of the alternate proposal framework across WE and CD settings on HumanEval and GSM8K, using multiple model pairs and CD temperatures. This tests the contribution of a central component beyond the retained proposal-length, weight and quality-speed analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run/seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing speedup values in Tables 2–4 are retained, but v2 adds parallel-baseline scores, raw throughput, APF ablations and NPU results. Table 10 reports 1.86x for WE-CoS on Llama-Vicuna/HumanEval. New ablations mostly favor APF, with an exception: Llama-2/GSM8K at T=1 gives 1.20x with APF versus 1.21x without it in Table 8.

T1.justification: The correctness proof, acceptance-rate bounds and speedup results retain the same mathematical substance, including Appendix A. Changes to E/C notation, token subscripts and Corollary 3.5 wording do not introduce substantive assumptions, results or proofs.

C1.justification: Both retain the same central contributions: sampling from arbitrary combined distributions, alternating proposers, extending to multiple models and accelerating decoding while preserving output quality. The headline 1.11x–2.23x claim is unchanged. Collaborative decoding terminology and realignment examples clarify the previously broad combination-function scope.

C2.justification: Explanations involving acceptance rates, task determinism, proposal length, combination weights and quality-speed tradeoffs are retained. The new appendix sections primarily introduce tables, without adding substantive interpretations or limitations.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies RTX 3090 hardware, A6000 hardware for Llama-Vicuna, and Ascend 910B3 hardware for the added tests. It also updates the advertised code location from Speculative-Ensemble to CoS. Existing hyperparameters and algorithm details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces the pre-/post-/during-inference ensemble taxonomy with ensembling, contrastive decoding and decoding-time realignment, adding and removing relevant references. It also recasts SCD from a rejected-token-only comparison to a special case of Naive-CoS, emphasizing general applicability, alternation and theoretical analysis as differentiators.

P1.justification: The opening motivation and related-work narrative are substantially rewritten around collaborative decoding, with systematic CoS/Naive-CoS terminology throughout the paper and appendices. v2 adds an invocation-count explanation and Appendix C.3–C.5, while retaining the overall main-section order.

P2.justification: Figure 2 gains a standard-decoding panel for comparison with alternation. Table 1 is reformatted, Tables 2–3 gain parallel-baseline rows, and six new tables display throughput, ablations and NPU measurements. Existing sensitivity and quality-speed plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The component ablations, additional comparators, NPU tests and hardware disclosure provide useful empirical support and reproducibility information missing from v1. Reporting inconsistencies limit the gain: for OPT at T=0 on HumanEval, Table 6 throughput implies about 3.34x speedup, whereas retained Table 4 reports 3.28x, without an explanation of differing conditions. The additions support a modest net improvement despite this unresolved inconsistency.
